api_testing-1.stem: Which tool is widely used to send and inspect API requests manually?
options: Postman
Photoshop
Excel
Wireshark

api_testing-2.stem: What should a test check about the response of a successful GET request?
options: The status code, headers and body
The status code and the response time only
The body, compared with the last response received
The headers and the size of the response
api_testing-2.explanation: The status code, headers and body content or schema.

api_testing-3.stem: Which API test is a good negative test?
options: Sending an invalid token and expecting 401
Sending a valid request and expecting 200
Repeating a valid request and expecting the same data
Sending a valid request after a long pause
api_testing-3.explanation: Sending invalid input or missing authentication and expecting a proper 4xx error.

api_testing-4.stem: How can Postman collections run automatically in a pipeline?
options: With the Newman command-line runner
By exporting them to a spreadsheet for the whole team
By emailing them to the developers
By sharing the screen during the meeting

api_testing-5.stem: What does contract testing verify between a consumer and a provider service?
options: That messages match the agreed contract between them
That both services use the same programming language and framework
That both services run on the same server
That both services have the same number of tests as the work grows
api_testing-5.explanation: That requests and responses match the agreed contract, so changes do not break the consumer.

ci_for_testing-1.stem: Why run automated tests in a CI pipeline?
options: To catch regressions early on every change for the business
To avoid writing some of the manual test cases
To make the application use less memory when it runs in most cases
To remove the need for code review
ci_for_testing-1.explanation: To catch regressions early on every change.

ci_for_testing-2.stem: Which of these is a common CI server?
options: Jenkins
Zeplin
Notion
Miro
One that passes and fails without a code change from the start
One that usually fails on the first run
One that takes more than a second to run each time
One that has no assertions at all
ci_for_testing-3.explanation: A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change.

ci_for_testing-4.stem: A suite of 2,000 UI tests takes two hours in CI. What is the best way to speed it up?
options: Run the tests in parallel on several workers
Run the tests just once a month
Remove the assertions from each test in the long run
Run the tests on a developer laptop
ci_for_testing-4.explanation: Run the tests in parallel across several machines or containers and keep only valuable UI tests.

options: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle
Testing just after the product is released
Testing with just the left half of the team
Testing the left side of each page
ci_for_testing-5.explanation: Testing earlier in the development lifecycle, for example unit and integration tests in CI.

performance_testing-1.stem: Which tool is commonly used for load testing web applications?
options: Apache JMeter
Selenium IDE
Postman collections
Cucumber

performance_testing-2.stem: What is the goal of a load test?
options: Measure behaviour under the expected number of users
Find spelling mistakes on the pages for the project within the team
Check that the colours meet the style guide at that stage
Verify that the code compiles on each machine in the team
performance_testing-2.explanation: To measure behaviour under expected levels of concurrent users.

performance_testing-3.stem: The average response time is 300 ms but the 95th percentile is 4 seconds. What does this show?
options: A share of users gets a much slower experience
Most users get a much slower experience
The average is wrong and should be recalculated
The test had too few users to be meaningful
performance_testing-3.explanation: Some users have a much slower experience; percentiles reveal outliers that the average hides.

performance_testing-4.stem: What is the difference between a load test and a stress test?
options: Load uses expected traffic, stress goes past the limit
Load uses one user, stress uses two users as the work grows
Load checks the design, while stress checks the colours
They are two names for the same test in most teams during the project
performance_testing-4.explanation: A load test uses expected load; a stress test pushes beyond it to find the breaking point.

performance_testing-5.stem: Throughput stops growing as users increase while response time climbs. What is the likely situation?
options: A resource is saturated and has become the bottleneck
The load generator has run out of virtual users
The system scales well and needs no change
The response times are cached and not real
performance_testing-5.explanation: A bottleneck: some resource (CPU, database connections, locks) is saturated.

test_automation_web-1.stem: Which tool automates browser actions for testing web applications?
options: Selenium
Figma
Jira
Maven

test_automation_web-2.stem: What is a locator in UI test automation?
options: An expression that finds an element on the page
A file that stores the test results
A server that runs the browser somewhere in the cloud
A report that lists the failed tests
test_automation_web-2.explanation: An expression such as an id, CSS selector or XPath that finds an element on the page.

test_automation_web-3.stem: A test clicks a button before the page has loaded and fails at random. What is the right fix?
options: Wait explicitly for the element to be clickable
Add a fixed pause of thirty seconds at that stage
Run the test again until it passes in a real project
Remove the click from the test
test_automation_web-3.explanation: Use explicit waits for the element or condition instead of fixed sleeps.

test_automation_web-4.stem: What is the Page Object Model?
options: A pattern that wraps each page's elements and actions in a class
A report format for test results
A way to record the screen while tests run for the project in a real project
A database of test data for each page at that stage in most teams
test_automation_web-4.explanation: A pattern that wraps each page's elements and actions in a class to reduce duplication.

test_automation_web-5.stem: Which tests are best candidates for automation?
options: Stable, repetitive checks that run on every release during the project
One-off tests of a design that will change next week
Tests that need human judgement about the look
Tests of features that nobody uses
test_automation_web-5.explanation: Stable, repetitive, high-value checks such as regression and smoke tests.

test_design_techniques-1.stem: What should a good bug report contain?
options: Steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, and environment
Steps to reproduce, the suspected cause in the code, and severity
Expected and actual results, and the developer to assign it to
A screenshot, the environment, and the date the error happened
test_design_techniques-1.explanation: Steps to reproduce, expected and actual result, environment and evidence such as screenshots.

options: Re-testing existing features after a change
Testing a new feature for the first time
Testing the system under very heavy load
Testing the changed code by reading it
test_design_techniques-2.explanation: Re-testing existing features after a change to make sure nothing broke.

test_design_techniques-3.stem: A field accepts ages from 18 to 60. Which values are the boundary values to test?
test_design_techniques-3.explanation: Boundary value analysis tests values at and around the limits: 17, 18, 60, 61.

options: Groups inputs treated alike and tests one value per group
Groups inputs treated alike and tests every value in each group
Tests only the values at the edges of each input range
Groups test cases by feature and runs one per feature
test_design_techniques-4.explanation: It groups inputs that the system should treat the same way and tests one value per group.

test_design_techniques-5.stem: Time is short and the release cannot move. How should you prioritise the tests?
options: Test the highest-risk and most-used features first
Test the features in the order they were built in practice
Test just the features that are easy to automate first
Skip testing and rely on user feedback after release
test_design_techniques-5.explanation: Risk-based testing: test the highest-risk and most-used features first.
